skill.name: budget-pacing-monitor
skill.description: Monitors live advertising spend against a planned budget curve. It reports pacing status, learning-phase limits, delivery drivers, and whether to hand off a reallocation decision.
skill.summary: Check whether a live campaign is spending on pace.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, relative documentation links, and descriptive advertising-analysis text. One documented ledger command interpolates a campaign placeholder without quoting or validation, which can permit shell command injection if executed with adversarial input. No prompt-injection language or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unquoted campaign value in the ledger command
remediation.suggestion: Do not construct a shell command from a campaign name. Pass it as a separately quoted argument through a non-shell process API, or restrict it to an allowlisted identifier format before execution.

content.value_statement: Live campaigns can overspend, underspend, or produce misleading signals during learning. This skill compares spend with a planned curve and gives a clear pacing verdict with a next action.
actual_capabilities: Compares cumulative campaign spend with an even, front-loaded, or back-loaded target curve.
Classifies pacing as On-track, Ahead, Behind, or Stalled.
Calculates percent-to-pace and projects end-of-flight spend from the current rate.
Checks whether learning-phase status makes a budget change unsafe.
Names likely delivery drivers using user-provided campaign export data.
Recommends a fire or hold reallocation trigger and a next check date.
limitations: Requires a user-provided campaign export with spend and flight information.
Does not access advertising platforms or dashboards by itself.
Does not calculate a new budget allocation or choose a bid strategy.
Projections depend on the target curve and the accuracy of the supplied data.

use_cases.title: Review a mid-flight campaign
use_cases.description: Check whether a campaign is ahead of or behind its planned spend curve before the next budget review.

use_cases.title: Investigate a spend spike
use_cases.description: Assess whether an early daily-cap hit is over-delivery and identify delivery signals to review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a stakeholder update
use_cases.description: Create a measured pacing summary with a projection, trigger decision, and next check date.

prompt_templates.title: Check a simple campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Check pacing for Campaign X. The daily budget is $200, the flight is 30 days, and day 9 has ended. Cumulative spend is $1,650. Use an even target curve.

prompt_templates.title: Review a lifetime budget
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this campaign pacing. Lifetime budget is $12,000 from August 1 through August 31. Today is August 18 and spend is $7,900. The target is front-loaded. State the pace, projection, and next check date.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose under-delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess under-delivery using this export summary: budget remaining $4,000, 70% of the flight elapsed, 42% spent, learning exited, low search volume, and no daily cap hit. Give the likely driver and reallocation trigger.

prompt_templates.title: Apply learning-phase protection
prompt_templates.prompt: Check pacing for a campaign at 135% of its planned curve. It is still in learning phase after a recent budget edit. Separate measured facts from estimates and decide whether to hold or fire a reallocation trigger.

output_examples.input: A 30-day even-paced campaign is on day 15 and has spent $2,700 of a $6,000 budget.
output: Pacing verdict: Behind at 90% of planned pace.
Learning status: Confirm before changing budget.
Action: Hold reallocation until learning status and recent delivery data are confirmed.

output_examples.input: A front-loaded flight has spent 68% of its budget after 45% of the flight, and learning has exited.
output: Pacing verdict: Ahead of the stated curve.
Projection: Review end-of-flight spend against the lifetime cap.
Action: Fire a reallocation review and set the next check date.

best_practices: Set the target curve before reviewing spend so the comparison reflects the original plan.
Use exported daily spend data and label every figure as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Confirm learning-phase status before acting on an apparent pacing gap.
anti_patterns: Do not judge pacing from a dashboard screenshot or a single total-spend value.
Do not change budget during learning phase based only on a short-term pace signal.
Do not present a projected end-of-flight result as measured performance.

faq.question: What data do I need?
faq.answer: Provide the campaign budget, flight dates, target curve, cumulative or daily spend, and learning-phase status when available.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to my ad account?
faq.answer: No. It uses data that you provide, such as a manually exported campaign report.

faq.question: What target curves are supported?
faq.answer: It supports even, front-loaded, and back-loaded spending plans.

faq.question: Can it change my budget?
faq.answer: No. It recommends whether a reallocation review is warranted and routes allocation work to a separate skill.

faq.question: Why does learning phase matter?
faq.answer: Budget changes during learning can reset optimization, so pacing signals may not support an immediate action.

faq.question: How accurate is the projection?
faq.answer: It is an estimate based on current delivery and the supplied plan. Changes in demand, bids, or targeting can change the result.
